assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray burst afterglows with an X-ray instrument and the follow-up optical identification settled a decades-old problem by showing that bursts are cosmological, among the most energetic events known. This is a clean, instrument-enabled discovery with lasting impact on high-energy astrophysics, and it opened the field of multi-messenger transient astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The decisive chain is the arcminute localisation by the wide-field and narrow-field X-ray instruments on a satellite (Costa, Frontera) and the rapid optical and redshift follow-up that fixed the distance scale (Kulkarni). That maps onto a plausible three-person configuration, although the optical follow-up involved other groups whose roles I cannot adjudicate from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Discovered in 1997 and confirmed by hundreds of afterglows, redshifts and supernova associations over nearly three decades. The interpretation is stable; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the satellite team and the optical/radio follow-up teams is not fully resolved by three names.
I have an instrumentation affinity with gamma-ray astronomy and have not independently verified details of the original discovery chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the subsequent association with a flaring blazar and with the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy at a kilometre-cubed detector built in Antarctic ice. It is a major experimental and conceptual achievement with clear lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Only one name is supplied. Halzen was a driving intellectual and project leader of the detector concept, but a detector of this scale is a large collaboration achievement, and a prize would normally want to recognise the experimental pioneers of the technique more broadly, which the supplied credit cannot support.
assessment.maturity: Evidence for the diffuse flux (2013), the blazar association (2018) and the Galactic plane (2023) have been confirmed by independent analyses, though source identification remains incomplete. Recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: A single-person prize for a large collaboration discovery is difficult to justify against the roles of other founders of the technique.
Only partial source identification so far; the nature of the diffuse flux is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field. It is original, clear, and has had very rapid impact across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: The theory (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the experimental demonstration (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators) form a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. Contributions by other experimental groups and earlier theorists are not among the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced since 2018, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated phases is still debated, so the physical interpretation is not yet settled. Timing is somewhat early but defensible.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconducting phase is unresolved.
Allocation between Bistritzer, MacDonald and other early theorists is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells established topological insulators as a distinct phase of matter with protected edge states. The concept reshaped band theory and materials research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theoretical formulation; Molenkamp led the first experimental demonstration. The proposed trio fits a theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other contributors to the HgTe prediction and three-dimensional topological insulators are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently across many materials and platforms over about two decades; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely to somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with other topological-insulator candidates on the list means the credit set could be drawn differently.
Some contributors to the HgTe prediction are outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with magic-wavelength trapping reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, a precision revolution that enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. Instrumental ingenuity and measurement science of the kind I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance to the extreme. A two-person prize is straightforward, though frequency-comb and trapped-ion clock contributions have already been honoured or sit outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories reproduce and now compare clocks at the 1e-18 level; the field is mature and the impact on metrology is well established.
uncertainties: The redefinition of the second has not happened yet, so the ultimate practical impact is still pending.
Other contributors to the lattice-clock concept may deserve credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution founded quantum cryptography and linked foundations of quantum mechanics to practical information security. The BB84 protocol and the entanglement-based protocol are original and have driven decades of experimental work and quantum networks.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the BB84 authors; Ekert proposed the entanglement-based scheme. The three-name configuration is natural, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated in the field and via satellites, but security of practical devices is an ongoing issue. The conceptual contribution is mature, though a recent prize on entanglement experiments partly overlaps.
uncertainties: Credit for early conjugate-coding ideas is not representable with the supplied names.
Possible perceived overlap with a recent prize on quantum entanglement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering provided a standard ruler that robustly anchors dark-energy and expansion-history measurements, independent of supernovae. Clear observational signature with lasting cosmological value.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detection in the SDSS luminous red galaxy sample (Eisenstein) and the contemporaneous 2dFGRS detection (Cole, Percival) are the decisive contributions, though both were large survey collaborations. The theoretical prediction of the feature is not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many surveys with increasing precision; recent evidence of possible evolving dark energy keeps the interpretation lively but does not undermine the standard-ruler measurement.
uncertainties: Credit is spread across large survey collaborations and early theory not named here.
Cosmology has been recognised repeatedly, so relative priority is a committee judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise controllable quantum many-body systems and quantum simulators, with proposals (Cirac, Zoller) and experimental demonstrations (Bloch, Greiner) that created a field bridging atomic physics and condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: A theory-plus-experiment configuration is plausible, but Greiner is left out of my three names and Jaksch's lattice proposal is not in the credited list, so the allocation is genuinely contestable.
assessment.maturity: Well established, with many independent groups and quantum-gas microscopes; yet the scientific payoff of simulation beyond classical tractability is still maturing.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit among four named people and uncredited proposers is uncertain.
Overlap with other quantum-simulation and quantum-computing candidates.
